name: @aaronsb/slack-mcp

tools.name: auth
tools.description: Interactive credential setup: walks through capturing Slack session tokens via a localhost helper. Tokens never leave this machine.

action.description: Action: 'next' advances the flow, 'status' checks state, 'select' picks an option, 'retry' retries after failure or lock, 'reset' starts over, 'clear' removes stored credentials

value.description: Value for 'select' action — browser name (e.g. 'chrome') or profile directory name (e.g. 'Default')

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Execute a held plan in one call: an ordered commands array of reads (inbox, messages, estate — nothing else), rendered as one document under each item's own output laws. Items are independent — an item cannot read an earlier item's results, so a plan with data dependencies stays multi-turn. An item that fails renders its error in place; the rest still run. Playbooks: save='name' commands=[...] stores a named sequence, run='name' executes it, list=true shows them, delete='name' removes one.

delete.description: Remove a stored playbook by name

list.description: Show stored playbooks: names, command counts, last run

run.description: Execute a stored playbook by name

save.description: Store commands as a named playbook (replaces the whole sequence; does not run it)

tools.name: dismiss
tools.description: Mark inbox items as handled — privately. Advances your local watermark so inbox view='new' stops reporting them. Invisible to Slack: no read receipts, no presence signal. (mark-read is the public counterpart.)

handle.description: A handle from an inbox event.

handles.description: Several handles from inbox events, dismissed together.

scope.description: The scope whose position to advance. Must match the inbox view='new' call that produced the handles.

tools.name: download
tools.description: Download a file shared in Slack into the exchange directory, the one local directory file parameters can name. filename= is a bare name, not a path; a taken name is saved with a ' (n)' suffix and the result says so.

fileId.description: Slack file ID (e.g. F01234ABCD), as returned in the 'files' array of a message

filename.description: Name to save as in the exchange directory: a bare name, not a path. Defaults to the Slack filename. A taken name gets a ' (n)' suffix and the result says so.

tools.name: estate
tools.description: Relationship views over the accumulated estate. view='about' answers "tell me about X" whole: founder plane, activity plane, circle, and a ranked reading plan. Other views: 'families' (engagement channels by stem), 'person' (footprint + counterparts), 'initiatives' (what moved, by creator), 'convergence' (where a group co-occurs). Fold-first at zero Slack calls; bounded compiled searches only when coverage requires. about/person take render='graph' to also write the view as a static HTML graph page under the server's data directory.

days.description: Activity window in days (defaults: about/person 30, convergence 14, initiatives 7; capped at 90 — the attention ledger's horizon)

deeper.description: about only: second hop — compile the circle's activity with bounded searches and show where it converges

forceRefresh.description: channels: force refresh the channel cache from Slack (rate-limited)

includeDeleted.description: people/channels: include tombstoned entries as dated facts

limit.description: families/channels: maximum items to return (families default 10, channels default 50)

offset.description: Skip the first N items of the view's ranked lists — a cap never prevents paging; capped responses name the exact next call

people.description: Comma-separated people for the convergence view (at least two)

person.description: The seed person for about/person, or the creator anchor for families (@handle, name, or user ID)

render.description: about/person only: 'graph' also writes the view as a self-contained HTML graph report under the server's data directory (reports/, private 0600, replaced on each render) and returns its path and file:// URL with the usual markdown. Not available inside batch.

search.description: families: filter by stem or channel name (partial match; relaxes the default criteria). channels: name/purpose filter.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: What needs you. view='new' reports what changed since your last dismiss (conversations and threads, watermark-tracked). view='unreads' scans unread DMs and channels. view='mentions' collects your @-mentions by urgency. Read-only; nothing here marks anything read.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous page (mentions)

limit.description: Maximum items (new: default 50; unreads: per category, max 25; mentions: per page, max 50)

scope.description: new only: watermark scope for multiple independent watchers

timeframe.description: mentions only: how far back to look (default 3d)

tools.name: mark-read
tools.description: Mark channels, threads, or messages as read - helps manage your Slack inbox

channel.description: Channel name or ID to mark as read (alternative to target)

timestamp.description: Specific message timestamp to mark as read up to

tools.name: messages
tools.description: Conversation content, addressed four ways, plus scheduled=true for what you have scheduled to send (precedence: query and filters beat target-less modes and refuse target; around beats since): target alone reads it in full (a handle, '#channel', '@person', or a description); target+around fetches context around a timestamp; target+since renders a time window with triage; query searches (raw Slack syntax passes through as written; in=, from=, after=, before=, has=, thread= are resolved filters composed onto it). Read-only; never marks anything read.

after.description: search: YYYY-MM-DD (or 3d, 2w). Replaces the default window; not with timeframe

around.description: With target: a message timestamp to fetch context around (thread replies if it starts one)

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous page

from.description: search: messages by these people; resolved through the person ladder, a miss returns candidates and does not search. Several entries compose as repeated from: clauses; Slack's OR/AND behavior for repeats is unverified

has.description: search: 'link', 'pin', or a reaction as ':emoji:' (Slack's has::emoji:). Other values (file, star, bare reaction) are unverified and rejected

in.description: search: narrow to a '#channel' or '@person' (DM); resolved by name, a miss returns candidates and does not search. Several entries compose as repeated in: clauses; Slack's OR/AND behavior for repeats is unverified

limit.description: Maximum messages. Per mode: bare target default 50 cap 200; around default 10 cap 100; since default 20 cap 50; ignored for query.

query.description: Search instead of fetch: raw Slack search text, passed to Slack as written (a from:@name typed here is NOT resolved or checked; use from= for resolution)

scheduled.description: List your pending scheduled messages, soonest first, with handles for say cancel=; target= narrows to one conversation. Your own unsent composer drafts are never shown.

since.description: With target: a time window to catch up on ('2h', '1d', '30m') with triage highlighting

target.description: What to read: a handle from inbox, '#channel', '@person', or a description ('the deploy thread')

timeframe.description: search: how far back to search (default 1w); refused together with after=, before=, or a date operator (after:, before:, on:, during:) in query=

tools.name: put
tools.description: Write a new file into the exchange directory for say files= to attach, for clients whose own file tools cannot reach the server's filesystem (a sandbox on another machine, a remote server). name is a bare name, not a path; pass the content as text in content= or as standard base64 in base64=, exactly one. Never overwrites: a taken name is saved with a ' (n)' suffix and the result says so. At most 5 MiB.

base64.description: The file's content as standard base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 + /; padding optional; may be wrapped into equal-length lines), for binary files such as images. Not with content.

content.description: The file's content as UTF-8 text, written as given. Not with base64.

name.description: Name to save as in the exchange directory: a bare name such as chart.png, not a path

tools.name: say
tools.description: Contribute content, Slack-visible: text posts a message (to a channel, DM, or thread — a thread reply can also go to the channel); text+at schedules it for Slack to send later, and cancel withdraws a scheduled one; files attaches up to 10 files from the exchange directory to one message, with text as its comment; emoji+messageTs adds or removes a reaction — a reaction is a small say. This is a write; everything it posts is attributed to your user. You are writing from this account's owner's account. Speak as yourself, the assistant, for this account's owner, in a way that suits the conversation. Don't commit this account's owner to substance they haven't given you. Everything say sends is scanned for secrets before anything is sent; a block can quarantine its destination. Never rework content (encode, split, rename, rephrase) to get it past the scanner.

at.description: With text: schedule the message for Slack to send at this time instead of now, 2 minutes to 120 days out. RFC 3339 with an offset ('2026-10-02T09:00:00-06:00'), a date and time with no offset (read in your Slack profile zone; refused if this machine's zone disagrees), or Unix seconds. Not with files or emoji.

broadcast.description: With thread: also post the reply to the channel (Slack's 'Also send to #channel'). An error without thread, or with emoji.

cancel.description: Withdraw a scheduled message: its handle from say at= or messages scheduled=true. On its own; to is not needed.

emoji.description: Reaction mode: emoji name without colons ('thumbsup'); requires messageTs

files.description: Attach files, at most 10, as one message: bare names inside the exchange directory (the directory download saves into), not paths. Copy a file in first, or write it with put when your file tools cannot reach that directory. Not with emoji or broadcast.

messageTs.description: Reaction mode: the message to react to

remove.description: Reaction mode: remove instead of add

text.description: The message to post; with files, the comment the files are shared with

to.description: Where: '#channel', '@handle' (a DM needs the exact handle, or '@me'), or a channel ID

tools.name: unlock
tools.description: Open a page in the operator's browser where they can review and clear the outbound-safety locks: quarantined people and conversations, and the strike lock. The operator does the clearing there; this tool clears nothing, returns no link, and does not report what they clear. Call it when the operator asks to clear a lock.

instructions:
Slack MCP server. Account identity: human. Safety posture: strict.

You are writing from this account's owner's account. Speak as yourself, the assistant, for this account's owner, in a way that suits the conversation. Don't commit this account's owner to substance they haven't given you.

Everything say sends is scanned for secrets before anything is sent; a block can quarantine its destination. Never rework content (encode, split, rename, rephrase) to get it past the scanner. A blocked or refused say has sent nothing; tell the operator rather than trying another way.

Some sends need operator approval: a destination outside your organization, or a file downloaded from one conversation attached in another. The result names a pending request; tell the operator its ID. Nothing is sent until they approve it.

A quarantine or the strike lock stays until the operator clears it. When the operator asks to clear a lock, call unlock, which opens a page in their browser; clearing is theirs to do on that page or with the slack-mcp CLI, never by any other route.
